result.title: One Teacher, Many Views: Reducing Reference Sensitivity in On-Policy Self-Distillation
result.summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) improves reasoning by training a model on its own trajectories with dense token-level supervision from a privileged copy conditioned on a reference solution. Existing methods typically use a single teacher distribution conditioned on the complete reference. We identify a limitation of this formulation: a reference is only one realization of the reasoning process. Although it provides evidence about the answer, it also encodes an ordering, phrasing, and solution path. Full-reference conditioning can therefore produce correct targets that depend excessively on information unavailable to the student at inference. We show that replacing one valid reference with another, while holding the problem and student state fixed, can substantially alter the teacher distribution, a phenomenon we call reference-induced target instability. To address this instability, we introduce Monte Carlo Privileged Distillation (MCPD), which models privileged context as a distribution over partial reference views and distills the marginal teacher distribution. MCPD evaluates the teacher under multiple views and averages the resulting next-token distributions. We show that this probability-space average is the exact target induced by minimizing the expected teacher-to-student KL divergence over privileged views. Across mathematical and scientific reasoning benchmarks, we show that MCPD produces more reference-consistent supervision and consistently improves over full-reference OPSD.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出现有 on-policy self-distillation 因教师依赖完整参考解而产生「reference-induced target instability」，提出 MCPD，将 privileged context 建模为部分参考视图的分布，并对多视图下教师的下一 token 分布取平均。
AI.relevance_reason: 其多视图边缘化教师监督可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、部分证据条件下的轨迹训练与目标构造提供借鉴，值得核查能否从参考解视图迁移到视觉视图或 latent 推理状态。
